title.fa: اراسموس و لوتر: اجماع مؤمنان در برابر یقین فردی (مناظرهٔ ارادهٔ آزاد)
title.en: Erasmus versus Luther: consensus of the faithful against individual certainty (the free-will debate)
title.nl: Erasmus tegenover Luther: consensus van de gelovigen tegenover individuele zekerheid (de vrije-wil-discussie)

summary.fa: در مناظرهٔ ۱۵۲۴–۱۵۲۵ بر سر ارادهٔ آزاد، اراسموس به «توافق مؤمنان» و سنت کلیسا تکیه کرد و لوتر به یقین حاصل از تجربهٔ ایمان و متن کتاب مقدس. مک‌کونیکا این اختلاف را اختلاف دو نظریهٔ مرجعیت و شناخت می‌داند.
summary.en: In the 1524–25 free-will debate Erasmus appealed to the consensus of the faithful and church tradition, Luther to certainty born of faith-experience and scripture. McConica reads it as a clash between two theories of authority and knowing.
summary.nl: In het vrije-wil-debat van 1524-25 beriep Erasmus zich op de consensus van de gelovigen en de kerkelijke traditie, Luther op zekerheid uit geloofservaring en de Schrift.

text.fa: لوتر و اراسموس ابتدا همدل بودند: هر دو با تقدم ارسطو و مدرسی مخالف بودند، کتاب مقدس را در کانون می‌دیدند و از سوءاستفاده در فروش آمرزش‌نامه انتقاد می‌کردند.
text.en: At first the two were allies: both opposed the primacy of Aristotle and scholasticism, put scripture at the centre, and criticised abuses in the sale of indulgences.
text.nl: At first the two were allies: both opposed the primacy of Aristotle and scholasticism, put scripture at the centre, and criticised abuses in the sale of indulgences.

text.fa: اراسموس از لوتر نخواست خاموش شود، بلکه برای شنیده‌شدن او و بررسی آرام عقایدش میان اهل علم و پرهیز از خشونت علیه او کوشید؛ اما از لحن جدلی و از آشوب‌آفرینی بیم داشت.
text.en: Erasmus did not ask Luther to be silent; he worked for a calm hearing among scholars and against violence towards him, yet feared the polemical tone and the disorder it could bring.
text.nl: Erasmus did not ask Luther to be silent; he worked for a calm hearing among scholars and against violence towards him, yet feared the polemical tone and the disorder it could bring.

text.fa: اراسموس Discourse on Free Will را در ۱۵۲۴ منتشر کرد (به پیشنهاد هنری هشتم)؛ لوتر در پایان ۱۵۲۵ با On the Enslaved Will پاسخ داد و از اراسموس برای رفتن سراغ اصل مسئله، نه فروعی چون برزخ، سپاس گفت.
text.en: Erasmus published the Discourse on Free Will in 1524, at Henry VIII's suggestion; Luther replied late in 1525 with On the Enslaved Will, thanking him for going to the heart of the matter rather than side issues like purgatory.
text.nl: Erasmus published the Discourse on Free Will in 1524, at Henry VIII's suggestion; Luther replied late in 1525 with On the Enslaved Will, thanking him for going to the heart of the matter rather than side issues like purgatory.

text.fa: محور استدلال اراسموس: روح‌القدس در ۱۳۰۰ سال کلیسا را در مسئله‌ای که لوتر جوهر انجیل می‌خواند بی‌خبر رها نکرده است؛ «کلیسا» یعنی توافق همهٔ مسیحیان و هیچ نهاد منفرد (پاپ، شورا) تضمین مطلق نیست.
text.en: Erasmus's core argument: the Holy Spirit would not have left the church in error for 1,300 years on a point Luther calls the essence of the Gospel; 'church' means the agreement of all Christians, and no single institution guarantees absolute truth.
text.nl: Erasmus's core argument: the Holy Spirit would not have left the church in error for 1,300 years on a point Luther calls the essence of the Gospel; 'church' means the agreement of all Christians, and no single institution guarantees absolute truth.

text.fa: به نظر اراسموس یقین دربارهٔ آموزه‌ها به گفت‌وگوی دیرپای جمع مؤمنان و عالمان وابسته است و قطعیت جزمی بدون توافق ممکن نیست؛ از این رو برخی مسائل را می‌شد در حالت تعلیق نگه داشت.
text.en: He held that certainty in doctrine depends on the long conversation of believers and scholars, so dogmatic finality is impossible without agreement; some questions could be left in suspension.
text.nl: He held that certainty in doctrine depends on the long conversation of believers and scholars, so dogmatic finality is impossible without agreement; some questions could be left in suspension.

text.fa: لوتر در مقابل از تجربهٔ شخصی درک «عدالت خدا» (رومیان ۱) به یقینی رسیده بود که او را ناگزیر از انتخاب میان آموزه‌ها می‌کرد؛ او اراسموس را بیش از اندازه انسان‌محور می‌دید.
text.en: Luther by contrast drew certainty from his personal insight into 'God's righteousness' (Romans 1), which forced him to choose between doctrines; he thought Erasmus too focused on man rather than God.
text.nl: Luther by contrast drew certainty from his personal insight into 'God's righteousness' (Romans 1), which forced him to choose between doctrines; he thought Erasmus too focused on man rather than God.

text.fa: اراسموس در مقدمه‌ای بر آثار هیلاریوس (۱۵۲۳) نوشت جوهر دین ما صلح و اتفاق نظر است؛ این وفاق‌گرایی در دعوا میان کاتولیک و پروتستان به‌عنوان بی‌موضعی یا کم‌دلی نکوهش می‌شد.
text.en: In his 1523 preface to Hilary he wrote that the essence of our religion is peace and unanimity, yet in the Catholic–Protestant quarrel this consensus-stance was condemned by both sides as lukewarmness.
text.nl: In his 1523 preface to Hilary he wrote that the essence of our religion is peace and unanimity, yet in the Catholic–Protestant quarrel this consensus-stance was condemned by both sides as lukewarmness.

text.fa: اینکه ارادهٔ آزاد و فیض به چه نسبت‌اند پرسشی الهیاتی است و داور تجربی ندارد؛ گزارش مک‌کونیکا موضع اراسموس را با همدلی می‌پروراند، در حالی که پژوهشگران پروتستان (مثلاً راپ) ادب و مهارت جدلی اراسموس را می‌پذیرند اما لوتر را عمیق‌تر می‌دانند.
text.en: How free will and grace relate is a theological question without empirical arbiter; McConica's account is sympathetic to Erasmus, while Protestant scholars such as Rupp grant his polemical skill yet judge Luther the deeper theologian.
text.nl: How free will and grace relate is a theological question without empirical arbiter; McConica's account is sympathetic to Erasmus, while Protestant scholars such as Rupp grant his polemical skill yet judge Luther the deeper theologian.
